sources.entry: NoMicSwitch - Pins the default audio input to the Mac's built-in microphone and locks the input volume, so AirPods never take it over.

summary.one_liner: NoMicSwitch is a small macOS daemon that pins the default audio input to the built-in microphone and locks input volume, reverting any change (such as AirPods taking over the mic) within milliseconds.
summary.what_it_does: The daemon registers three CoreAudio property listeners: default input device changes, input volume changes, and device connect/disconnect events. When the default input moves away from the chosen device, it switches it back; when input volume is lowered, it raises it back to the configured level (default 100%). It can pin any input device by UID, with --list showing available UIDs, and --no-volume leaves volume alone. The process sleeps between events, and the README reports 0.0% idle CPU and about 14 MB RAM on macOS 26. Installation is a dependency-free curl one-liner that fetches a prebuilt universal binary and checks its SHA-256, with Homebrew and source build options also given. It runs as a LaunchAgent so it restarts at login and after crashes.
use_cases: stop AirPods from taking over the Mac microphone
keep the MacBook built-in mic as default input
prevent Zoom or Teams from switching the mic
pin a USB microphone as the default input on macOS
avoid low-quality AirPods headset mode in calls
notable: Event-driven: sleeps between CoreAudio notifications, so idle CPU is zero
Reverts changes in under 100 ms rather than polling every few seconds
Pins devices by stable UID, not localized device name
Dependency-free one-line installer that verifies a SHA-256 checksum
Unlicense (public domain) with README in English, Portuguese and Spanish
caveats: Cannot prevent changes, only revert them, because macOS has no API to lock the default input device
While the daemon runs you cannot select another microphone by hand; you must pause the service first
Tested on macOS 26 on Apple Silicon; README says macOS 12 or newer should work, and older SDKs may need a symbol rename
No .pkg or .app; the binary is ad-hoc signed, not Developer ID signed
